name: move only the spaces and get another sentence
one_line: The letters keep their order and only the spaces move, so counting the letters on each side says whether an answer can be right.
how: Open with one worked example, because nothing else opens this form. RI drawn under AL over GO is said as «RI sotto AL su GO» and written «risotto al sugo», thirteen letters either way. Print both readings with their word lengths, 2 5 2 2 2 and 7 2 4. Then give a run of letters with no spaces and its length — CHIAMAMARCO, eleven — and ask for it to be respaced into something sayable. Say what makes an answer wrong: same letters, same order, none added and none dropped. Count both sides yourself before printing. A synonym helps where a word will not split: seggiola splits and sedia does not.

knobs.knob: whether a worked example opens it
knobs.effect: With one solved example the form is understood at once and needs no explaining. Without it, no statement of the rule works, and the person fails not at the puzzle but at knowing what is being asked.

knobs.knob: whether the two readings share their letters
knobs.effect: Respaced, the letter counts on both sides have to agree and the sheet checks itself by counting. Where nothing is respaced and only the sense changes, the diagram has one side and that check is gone.
Straight, the letters shown are described and split. Through a synonym, the thing has to be renamed before it can be split: two small steps each with its own check, instead of one step with none.
Given the letters and asked for the reading, the person respaces. Given the reading and asked for the letters, the person composes. The check is the same count either way round.

where_the_work_is: In the run of letters, which has to respace into something sayable, and that is found by hand. The counting that verifies it is mechanical and can be done by anybody, afterwards and in a minute.
breaks: The layout of the shown letters is half the game — above, below, inside — so it needs a page and dies on 800x480, where a single line has no above and no below. Scanned back it reads if the letters are large. A model can count the letters of an answer, which is comparing two strings, and cannot produce the string at all; every one printed has to be built and counted by hand.
